s: Deep Ellum's cult BBQ pilgrimage, lines and all
w: What started as a stall in the Dallas Farmers Market moved to a permanent Deep Ellum room and grew into the city's defining barbecue pilgrimage -- smoky, well-rested brisket, links and ribs, and a line out the door most weekends that regulars treat as part of the ritual rather than a deterrent.
_facts: Located at 2702 Main Street, Deep Ellum, Dallas, TX 75226
Started as a stall inside the Dallas Farmers Market before opening this permanent location
Known for brisket, house-made sausage and ribs
Regularly draws long weekend lines, treated locally as part of the experience

s: a low-key, high-precision BBQ spot serious pitmasters rank among Texas's best
w: A modest strip-mall-adjacent smokehouse in Farmers Branch, north of the city, that doesn't chase the crowds Pecan Lodge draws but earns just as much respect from serious Texas BBQ obsessives. Limited hours, sells out when the meat's gone, and rewards the regulars who know exactly when to show up.
_facts: Located at 13628 Gamma Rd, Farmers Branch/Dallas, TX 75244
Open limited hours, Wednesday through Friday, until the meat sells out
Frequently cited by BBQ enthusiasts among the best in Texas despite a low profile
Featured in the Michelin Guide Texas

s: the 1918 Tex-Mex original, still serving the Wednesday enchilada special
w: Founded in 1918 by Mexican immigrant Mike Martinez, El Fenix is credited as one of the birthplaces of Tex-Mex cuisine and is the oldest Mexican restaurant chain in the US. This flagship, rebuilt on McKinney Avenue in 1965, still packs a lunch line for its combination plates and the long-running Wednesday enchilada dinner special.
_facts: Flagship location at 1601 McKinney Avenue, Dallas, TX 75202
Founded 1918 (as a renaming of a 1916 café), making it the oldest Mexican restaurant chain in the US
Widely credited as one of the originators of Tex-Mex cuisine
Known for its long-running Wednesday cheese enchilada dinner special

s: the vine-covered Design District cafe that helped build Dallas's specialty coffee scene
w: Founded in 2012, Ascension's original Design District location -- a cafe tucked behind a wall of vines on Oak Lawn Avenue -- helped set the template for Dallas's modern specialty coffee culture. Now a small local chain, this is still the spot locals point to as the original.
_facts: Original location at 1621 Oak Lawn Ave, Dallas, TX 75207, in the Design District
Credited as an early driver of Dallas's specialty coffee scene
Has since expanded to multiple Dallas-Fort Worth locations

s: a downtown food hall in the AT&T Discovery District with a rotating mix of local vendors
w: A modern food hall inside downtown's AT&T Discovery District, gathering a rotating roster of local vendors and stalls under one roof -- a casual, varied counterpoint to Dallas's standalone destination restaurants, and an easy stop while wandering the plaza's fountains and outdoor screen.
_facts: Located at 211 S Akard St, Dallas, TX 75202, inside the AT&T Discovery District
Food hall format with a rotating mix of local restaurant vendors
Adjoins the AT&T Discovery District's public plaza and outdoor screen
